label: D2 arrival at S2 while the policy is not leaning toward a2
explanation: Fires only at D2 and only when the reached state is S2: there are zero activations at D1, at GO, or at D2 with S1. Within S2 arrivals (17% of which are active), it fires when the arrival is surprising or unfavourable for a2, meaning the agent does not currently favour a2. That covers rare S2 arrivals after choosing a1 (rate 6% vs 1.7% for common), S2 reached while S1 is the hidden good state, and S2 reached after an unrewarded previous trial. The strongest activations come from repeated unrewarded common a2->S2 trials when S1 is good, often right before the agent switches to a1. A good summary is the model policy logit at that D2 step, choice = logit(a1)-logit(a2) > -1.5 (not strongly committed to a2), which gets 95% of activation mass but only 48% precision. Magnitude grows with choice (top choice bins cover nearly all top-quartile activations). The rate also drops sharply over the episode (7.5% of steps in trials 0-9 vs 0.3% in trials 90-99), and adding ep_trial<50 lifts F1 to 0.67. The feature is silent whenever the agent is strongly committed to a2 (choice < -4.4) or the state is S1. Recorded predicate uses only observed state plus the model internal policy logit; no future variables.
